title: Interface / Link Down
keywords: link down interface GE port fiber cable disconnect
root_cause: Physical layer failure — either a fiber cut, a failed SFP transceiver, or the remote-end radio unit lost sync.
recommended_action: Check optical Rx/Tx levels on the SFP first. If levels are within spec, escalate to a field technician for a physical link inspection.

title: SFP Rx Power Low
keywords: sfp rx power low threshold optical
root_cause: Optical attenuation is creeping up, usually from a dirty connector, a bend in the fiber, or transceiver aging.
recommended_action: Trigger a remote SFP diagnostics poll and log the trend. If Rx power has degraded more than 3dB over 7 days, auto-open a maintenance ticket.

title: Temperature Warning Spike
keywords: temperature warning spike thermal fan overheating
root_cause: Short-lived thermal spike, most often caused by a blocked vent, a fan running below expected RPM, or a brief HVAC issue in the cabinet room.
recommended_action: Auto-restart the cooling fan controller and re-poll temperature in 5 minutes. Only escalate if the spike persists past two polling cycles.

title: Radio Link Degraded — Interference
keywords: radio link degraded interference microwave frequency
root_cause: Co-channel or adjacent-channel interference from a nearby transmitter, or seasonal fading affecting the microwave path.
recommended_action: Do not auto-remediate. Frequency changes affect a live service-affecting path — escalate to the RF planning team with the interference log attached.

title: Fan Speed Variance
root_cause: Minor mechanical variance in fan RPM, typically within normal tolerance and self-correcting.
recommended_action: Log and suppress. No action needed unless variance recurs more than 5 times in 24 hours.
